content:
Hello, I'm Jeremiah. I introduced myself here.

I opened PR #41508 with ~150 lemmas dumped across order theory, analysis, category theory, the works, without discussing it here first. That was the wrong way to do it and I appreciate the feedback I got.

The work: a verifier-mediated learning architecture. No neural network. No training. A bounded grammar proposes candidate abstractions, a hard verifier (the Lean kernel) accepts or rejects each. Details: https://github.com/sumofagents/manifold-destiny

I pointed it at mathlib's full theorem set and asked it to find duality gaps, lemmas whose dual (order-dual, left-right, preimage-image) was missing. It found and kernel-verified over 150 new ones.

To the reviewer's points, directly:

  • Novelty: I checked each lemma is absent at the statement level (isDefEq) against all ~530K constants at current master. Zero matches. But I welcome anyone double-checking. If something's already there under a different name, pull it.

  • Style + compile: fixed. Proof-level opens, simp only terminals, ad-style docstrings, all gone. Everything compiles inline in its real module via lake env lean at master.

  • Scope: going to keep it to one area per PR from here.

The question: is the community open to small, scoped, properly-styled PRs from this? And is verifier-mediated discovery of symmetry-gap lemmas worth pursuing, or is this already covered by existing automation?

These are just the first batch. The architecture also proves things directly, not just finds duals. I'll keep them coming as they become clear and validated.

Worth noting on the paper: Lean is one of three domains it's demonstrated on. The same loop runs on quantum entanglement data. The grammar constructs the angle-difference invariant from raw two-qubit measurement counts without being told to look for it, and a real Bell test (CHSH violation on a 156-qubit superconducting processor) confirms it. So it works in both classical and quantum realms under one mechanism. The mathlib lemmas are the Lean-domain instance of the same thing that recovers entanglement structure in the quantum domain.

Paper with all three domains, code, and reproduction receipts: https://github.com/sumofagents/manifold-destiny

I can drop a small clean sample (one area, fully building) here for feedback before anything else.

Thanks all, looking forward to helping push the understanding of discovery.

I don't think this is useful. There is already the @[to_dual] annotation to automatically generates instances of many dual lemmas, and while some useful dual lemmas may be missing, many of the ones I spot checked seem unnecessary or trivial and the poor style/file placement ensure it'll consume more reviewer time than they're worth.

Thank you for your feedback.
Can you elaborate what you mean by poor style/file placement? Would help me learn how to use this tool to be more impactful.
